_comment: #492. The Mission needed TWO templates or it would have been 100% commercial:
storefront_mission_tiled is the only Mission preset design #452 §3 names that has a generator,
and a district whose single template carries a shopfront dresses every house as a shop. This
is the residential companion, and library.json's districtTemplateWeights makes it the
overwhelming majority (10:1 over mission_storefront).
GROUND FLOOR: door (exact) + garage (rule), the same arrangement and the same numbers as
noe_valley_victorian, because it is the same schema constraint and the same two parts.
_exactMarks is written by PlaceExact and read by PlaceProcedural, so exclusion runs
exact -> procedural ONLY: a floor supports any number of exacts plus AT MOST ONE rule (#475,
lifting it is #491). The garage is the rule because only a rule can be width-gated -
count = floor(spanMeters / spacing) is computed before countMin/countMax, so countMin 0 with
spacingMeters 4.0 across a 0.76 span withholds the garage below a 5.26 m frontage, and
avoidExact + minSpacingMeters 2.0 withholds it below 5.13 m; a 2.53 m garage and a 1.29 m door
would only touch below 4.90 m, so the pair cannot overlap at any facade width.
WHAT IT DOES NOT REUSE. design #452 §3 marks bay_noe_slanted (slanted bay) and
cornice_noe_bracketed (bracketed gingerbread) EXCLUSIVE to Noe Valley, and the other two
shipped cornices exclusive to Sunset/Parkside and South of Market. Borrowing one would blur
the districts, which is the one thing the exclusive list exists to prevent - so this template
carries no bay and no roofPart. The Mission's own remaining §3 pieces (folding scissor gate,
mural band) have no generator yet; when they land they belong here.
NOT RENDERED. `Mission` is outside the play-area map.osm bbox (chunks_wintest is 1002
buildings, all Glen Park), so this template has never been looked at in the Editor - the same
reason #475 declined to add it. What is verified is the authored data: TemplateWiringTests.
